name: Sicula
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Whatmough, Joshua. 1937. The Foundations of Roman Italy. London: Methuen. (archive.org scanned of the Digital Library of India scan, item;ernet.dli.2015.80028)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sect. 8 'The Sicel dialect' (pp. 365-366) lists inscriptions, coin legends, glosses and names; no prosody. Only tangential remark p. 336: the e>i shift in the ethnonym Siculi (cf. sequor) happened 'in the first syllable (which was the accented syllable at the date when the change took place)' -- an etymological aside on the name, not a description of Siculian word stress.
